subject: general
question: According to the Global Peace Index 2025, which of the following countries at the bottom, indicating the least peaceful nation?
solution:
p>The correct answer is __**Russia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Global Peace Index (GPI) 2025**, **Russia** is ranked at the bottom of the list, indicating it as the least peaceful nation among the provided options due to its sustained **military aggression** and **internal suppression**.
 
• The index is an annual publication by the **Institute for Economics and Peace (IEP)**, a global think tank based in **Sydney, Australia**, which evaluates **163 independent states and territories**.
 
• Russia's ranking has deteriorated significantly since the full-scale **invasion of Ukraine** in **February 2022**, leading to massive increases in **battlefield deaths** and **military expenditure**. ***Hence, the statement regarding Russia is correct.***
 
• The evaluation is based on three thematic domains: **Societal Safety and Security**, **Ongoing Domestic and International Conflict**, and **Militarization**.
 
• While **Yemen**, **Sudan**, and **Syria** have consistently been among the most violent regions, the intensity of **international conflict** and **geopolitical isolation** has moved Russia to the bottom tiers of the index in the **2025** report.
 
• Russia’s score is negatively impacted by high levels of **political instability**, **violent demonstrations**, and a surge in **internal security** measures to maintain control during wartime.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure of the GPI**:
 
 
• The index was first launched in **May 2007** and remains the world's leading measure of global peacefulness, covering **99.7% of the world's population**.
 
• It utilizes **23 qualitative and quantitative indicators**, such as **homicide rates**, **access to weapons**, and **refugee populations**.
 
 
 
• **Most Peaceful Nations**:
 
 
• **Iceland** has consistently held the title of the **most peaceful country** in the world since **2008**.
 
• Other highly peaceful nations often include **Denmark**, **Ireland**, **New Zealand**, and **Austria**, which benefit from **low corruption** and **high transparency**.
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact of Violence**:
 
 
• The **IEP** calculates the **economic cost of violence**, which includes the loss of **GDP** and expenses related to **military** and **internal security**.
 
• For nations like **Russia** and **Ukraine**, the economic impact of the **war** has exceeded **30% to 60% of their respective GDPs** in recent years.
 
 
 
• **Regional Trends**:
 
 
• The **Middle East and North Africa (MENA)** region remained the least peaceful region for several years, though **Europe** has seen the largest regional deterioration in peace due to the **war in Eurasia**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Negative vs. Positive Peace**:
 
 
• **Negative Peace** is defined as the **absence of violence** or fear of violence, which is what the **GPI** primarily measures.
 
• **Positive Peace** refers to the **attitudes, institutions, and structures** that create and sustain peaceful societies, such as a **well-functioning government** and **sound business environment**.
 
 
 
• **Conflict in Sudan and Yemen**:
 
 
• **Sudan** experienced a sharp decline in peacefulness following the outbreak of **civil war** in **April 2023** between the **Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF)** and the **Rapid Support Forces (RSF)**.
 
• **Yemen** remains a critical humanitarian concern, though it has seen slight fluctuations in its ranking depending on the intensity of the **Houthi-led conflict**.
 
 
 
• **Militarization Domain**:
 
 
• This domain measures the **military capacity** of a country, including **nuclear weapons capability** and **arms exports**. **Russia** scores very poorly in this domain due to its status as a major **nuclear power** and its massive **arms production**.
